What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
We know that for any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(-4,6).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
(x+4)^{2}=4p(y-6).
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(4,-6),$ so we can substitute $x=4$ and $y=-6$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2} & =4p(y-6) \\ (4+4)^{2} & =4p(-6-6) \\ 64 & =-48p \\ p & =-\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{2} & =4p(y-6) \\ (x+4)^{2} & =4(-\frac{4}{3})(y-6) \\ (x+4)^{2} & =-\frac{16}{3}(y-6).\end{aligned}
$$
